title: Editor quitting project too soon sometimes
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.6.3.stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.3.stable - Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS 24.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon 760M Graphics (radeonsi, phoenix, LLVM 20.1.2, DRM 3.57, 6.8.0-117-generic) - AMD Ryzen 5 7640U w/ Radeon 760M Graphics (12 threads) - 13.45 GiB memory

### Issue description

In a very tiny script, the editor quits too soon...sometimes.
It is not consistent but should be able to be reproduced with a few attempts.
Noticed this while getting GUIDs for #119785, #119786, #119814, #119817
I used `Run Current Scene` to avoid having to make a new project just for this.

I have seen three different cases so far:
- the print line is not executed but everything else is normal
- the print line is not executed and the text above `Debugging process stopped` is missing 
- the print line is executed and everything else is normal (this is the expected result)

It seems to "help" to comment out the print line for one run, then change it back but that could also be a coincidence.

### Steps to reproduce

Have a script that does this in `_ready`:
- print something (should probably not be something that has to be awaited but did not test this)
- then immediately quits

You don't even need a controller for the MRP. If none is connected, you know it executed the print line when you get an error.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

```GDSCript
extends Node2D

func _ready() -> void:
	print(Input.get_joy_guid(0))
	get_tree().quit()
```
